items.effect: Inferred: the 19,400 week was a one-off burst, so the top of funnel has returned to baseline and sample requests should thin through the two to three week lag.
items.action: Inferred: set and log an explicit weekly invite baseline instead of treating 19,400 as the norm.

items.effect: Inferred: first-touch volume fell 73 percent, which is the strongest leading indicator of fewer sample requests from mid-October.
items.action: Inferred: hold the DM baseline steady for two weeks before judging any downstream change.

items.effect: Inferred: the count fell with send volume, but the reply rate rose to 0.39 percent from 0.28 percent, so per-send response did not weaken.
items.action: Inferred: rewrite the first DM line against the top umbrella and bidet hooks and retest on one list.

items.effect: Inferred: the campaign sits below its 0.6 target and the 1.0 break-even, losing roughly 590 USD on 1,146.20 USD of weekly spend.
items.action: Inferred: keep it disabled and move budget to Screen Door (ROI 2.322) and Bidet 7/6 (ROI 1.787).

items.effect: Inferred: 66 of 300 requests were rejected, a mild rise that suggests the inbound default-approve discipline is loosening.
items.action: Inferred: reapply the default-approve rule on inbound requests and recheck the rate weekly.

items.effect: Inferred: 52 To Review plus 80 Content Pending against only 10 Posted means the supply cohort is stalled at review and content stages.
